newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money trade stalls on kuna shortage.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money trade stalls on kuna shortage.

text.p: The Croatian money trade stalled on Thursday morning due to a kuna shortage while banks sought more funds for pre-Christmas cash spending, dealers said.
"There were some indications yesterday that demand would rise and there is so little money available," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
She put the morning gap at 39 million kuna as some lenders were also withdrawing earlier loans.
New borrowings totalled only 12.5 million kuna, all done at a call money rate of 9.0 percent.
But liquidity was expected to improve on Friday after the central bank pays kuna to the banks that sold it foreign exchange on Wednesday.
Wednesday's overnight trade was put at 25.5 million kuna, compared to none a day earlier when all banks were positive. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
